comment: NPC BEHAVIOUR PROFILES. Vocabulary (which intents exist) is code; character (which intents a creature is allowed, how much it wants each, how far it sees, what range it likes, how often it swings) is this file. A mob sidecar opts in with "behavior": "<name>"; the dev overlay's AI panel switches it at runtime and can write this file back. Hot-reloads on R alongside materials, glyphs and items. The full schema, and the reasoning behind every field, is at the top of src/game/ai_behavior.cpp and src/game/ai_behavior.h.
notes: An intent ABSENT from a profile's "intents" map has weight 0 and is disabled — that is the enable flag, deliberately not a second boolean nobody would keep in sync. An empty profile is a blind, immobile statue, so a creature only ever does what its JSON asked for. Ranges are WORLD VOXELS centre-to-centre (kVoxelMeters = 0.10, so 10 voxels is a metre); cadences are 30 Hz sim TICKS.

profiles.comment: THE SPACING FIXTURE'S PROFILE (src/test/selftest_mob.cpp GateCrowd). Mobile, hostile and it WANTS the target -- which is the whole of what a crowd test needs -- with no `attack` intent and no styles at all, so it walks into the scrum and never swings. It exists because `crowd` is a gate about PERSONAL SPACE and a fixture of four ARMED duelists converging on one point is a knife fight: they are held 3.6 voxels apart by the very feature under test, their swords are 8 voxels long, and they are inside each other's arcs by construction. Measured 2026-09-15, with a sword that finally connects (the sweep's probe no longer dies inside the wielder): 11 attack requests, 54 cut ticks and one of the four dead, on a gate whose spacing numbers were passing perfectly. Friendly fire is `duel`'s subject and it has its own gate; asserting it here made the spacing claim hostage to it. Same reason `training_dummy` exists three entries down.
profiles.name: crowder
profiles.label: Crowder (spacing fixture)

profiles.comment: A dummy of a DIFFERENT FACTION, so a hostile creature will actually pick it as a target. `dummy` is faction "monster" and so is everything that would swing at it, which makes it a training partner nobody attacks. Otherwise identical: blind, passive, immobile.

profiles.comment: A duelist of the OPPOSING faction, so two of them fight. Identical to `duelist` apart from the faction name.
profiles.name: duelist_blue
profiles.label: Duelist (blue)

profiles.comment: THE WALKING DEAD. Every style it owns is a NATURAL WEAPON (docs/PLAN_impact_unarmed.md), so a disarmed zombie is exactly as dangerous as an armed one -- which is the whole feature: it bites and it punches, and losing a hand costs it one style rather than all of them. It is the first profile whose reach is not the whole story: `bite_lunge` states 22 of its own, and MobSystem::AttackReachOf hands the LONGER of the two to the arbiter, so the creature commits from three body-lengths out and the leap closes the gap. Putting 22 here instead would have it stand off at 22 to punch, which is the coupling the per-style reach exists to break.
profiles.//character: SLOWER AND RECKLESS. A 48-tick cadence against the duelist's 34 (a zombie winds up, it does not fence), a band that starts INSIDE the duelist's (2..7 against 7..11) and almost no retreat or circling -- the dead do not give ground and they do not look for an angle. `disengageTicks` 0 for the same reason: a duelist hits and steps off, a zombie hits and keeps coming. Sight is shorter (34) and the fov is the full 360, because it does not need to be looking at you.
profiles.name: zombie
profiles.label: Zombie
